web.title: mc admin heal - MinIO AIStor Documentation
web.description:
# mc admin heal
The `mc admin heal` command scans for objects that are damaged or corrupted and heals those objects.

`mc admin heal` is resource intensive and typically not required as a manual process, even after drive failures or corruption events.

As a part of normal operations, MinIO AIStor:

- automatically heals objects damaged by silent bit rot corruption, drive failure, or other issues on each `POST` or `GET` operation.
- performs periodic background object healing using the [scanner](https://docs.min.io/aistor/reference/aistor-server/scanner/).
- aggressively heals objects after drive replacement.

Refer to [Object Healing](https://docs.min.io/aistor/operations/core-concepts/healing/) for more details on how MinIO AIStor heals objects.

## [Anchor to: Syntax](https://docs.min.io/aistor/reference/cli/admin/mc-admin-heal/#syntax)  Syntax
```shell
mc admin heal [FLAGS] TARGET             \
                      [--all-drives, -a] \
                      [--cross-pool]     \
                      [--dry-run, -n]    \
                      [--force]          \
                      [--pool int]       \
                      [--recursive, -r]  \
                      [--remove]         \
                      [--scan "string"]  \
                      [--set int]        \
                      [--verbose, -v]
```

## [Anchor to: Parameters](https://docs.min.io/aistor/reference/cli/admin/mc-admin-heal/#parameters)  Parameters
### [Anchor to: --cross-pool](https://docs.min.io/aistor/reference/cli/admin/mc-admin-heal/#--cross-pool)  --cross-pool
Combines objects that have become split across pools.

### [Anchor to: --pool](https://docs.min.io/aistor/reference/cli/admin/mc-admin-heal/#--pool)  --pool
_Optional_

Heals only the given pool, specified as an integer. Pools are numbered from 1.

### [Anchor to: --scan](https://docs.min.io/aistor/reference/cli/admin/mc-admin-heal/#--scan)  --scan
_Optional_

Selects the healing scan mode.

The `uncommitted` mode heals one erasure set at a time. Pass both `--pool` and `--set` when you specify this mode.

web.title: Decommission Aged Hardware - MinIO AIStor Documentation
web.description:
# Decommission Aged Hardware
MinIO AIStor supports decommissioning and removing server pools from a deployment with two or more pools. To decommission, there must be at least one remaining pool with sufficient available space to receive the objects from the decommissioned pools.

Each listed pool immediately enters a read-only status, but draining occurs one pool at a time.

The procedures on this page decommission and remove one or more server pools from a MinIO AIStor deployment with _at least_ two server pools.

## [Anchor to: Online decommissioning with zero downtime](https://docs.min.io/aistor/operations/scaling/decommission/#online-decommissioning-with-zero-downtime)  Online decommissioning with zero downtime
### [Anchor to: Why this matters](https://docs.min.io/aistor/operations/scaling/decommission/#why-this-matters)  Why this matters
MinIO AIStor decommissions an entire server pool, handles all data migration automatically, and keeps the cluster fully available to applications throughout the process.

### [Anchor to: Hot pool reload for config.yaml deployments](https://docs.min.io/aistor/operations/scaling/decommission/#hot-pool-reload-for-configyaml-deployments)  Hot pool reload for config.yaml deployments
```shell
kill -HUP $(pgrep minio)
```

```shell
systemctl reload minio
```

If a [rebalance](https://docs.min.io/aistor/reference/cli/admin/mc-admin-rebalance/) is running, MinIO AIStor rejects a reload that adds a pool. Stop the rebalance with `mc admin rebalance stop ALIAS` and send `SIGHUP` again, or restart the cluster with the new pool configuration.

A reload that also adds a pool stays rejected while a rebalance is active.

## [Anchor to: Considerations](https://docs.min.io/aistor/operations/scaling/decommission/#considerations)  Considerations
### [Anchor to: Pool names for config.yaml deployments](https://docs.min.io/aistor/operations/scaling/decommission/#pool-names-for-configyaml-deployments)  Pool names for config.yaml deployments
```shell
mc admin decommission start myaistor/ hash:a10f38e84ec12b
```

web.description:
# Core Operational Concepts [Permalink to this heading](https://minio.community/community/minio-object-store/operations/concepts.html#core-operational-concepts)
## [How does a distributed MinIO deployment work?](https://minio.community/community/minio-object-store/operations/concepts.html#id3) [Permalink to this heading](https://minio.community/community/minio-object-store/operations/concepts.html#how-does-a-distributed-minio-deployment-work)
### [How does MinIO manage multiple virtual or physical servers?](https://minio.community/community/minio-object-store/operations/concepts.html#id4) [Permalink to this heading](https://minio.community/community/minio-object-store/operations/concepts.html#how-does-minio-manage-multiple-virtual-or-physical-servers)
If one server pool goes down, MinIO halts I/O to all pools until the cluster resumes normal operations. You must restore the pool to working operation to resume I/O to the deployment.

```
minio server https://minio{1...4}.example.net/mnt/disk{1...4}

|                    Server Pool                |
```

### [How does MinIO link multiple server pools into a single MinIO cluster?](https://minio.community/community/minio-object-store/operations/concepts.html#id5) [Permalink to this heading](https://minio.community/community/minio-object-store/operations/concepts.html#how-does-minio-link-multiple-server-pools-into-a-single-minio-cluster)
```
minio server https://minio{1...4}.example.net/mnt/disk{1...4} \
             https://minio{5...8}.example.net/mnt/disk{1...4}

|                    Server Pool                |
```

### [Can I change the size of an existing MinIO deployment?](https://minio.community/community/minio-object-store/operations/concepts.html#id6) [Permalink to this heading](https://minio.community/community/minio-object-store/operations/concepts.html#can-i-change-the-size-of-an-existing-minio-deployment)
For deployments which have multiple server pools, you can [decommission](https://minio.community/community/minio-object-store/operations/deployments/baremetal-decommission-server-pool.html#minio-decommissioning) the older pools and migrate that data to the newer pools in the deployment. MinIO intends decommissioning for use with removing older pools with aged hardware, and not as an operation performed regularly within any deployment.

If you decommission the `minio-{5...8}` pool, you cannot add a new pool with the same node numbering.

## [How does MinIO provide availability, redundancy, and reliability?](https://minio.community/community/minio-object-store/operations/concepts.html#id10) [Permalink to this heading](https://minio.community/community/minio-object-store/operations/concepts.html#how-does-minio-provide-availability-redundancy-and-reliability)
### [MinIO Implements Bit Rot Healing to Protect Data At Rest](https://minio.community/community/minio-object-store/operations/concepts.html#id12) [Permalink to this heading](https://minio.community/community/minio-object-store/operations/concepts.html#minio-implements-bit-rot-healing-to-protect-data-at-rest)
MinIO can also perform bit rot checks and healing using the [MinIO Scanner](https://minio.community/community/minio-object-store/operations/concepts/scanner.html#minio-concepts-scanner). However, scanner bit rot checking is **off** by default. Active bit rot healing during scanner has a high performance impact in comparison to the low probability of bit rot affecting multiple object shards distributed across multiple drives and nodes. The automatic checks during normal operations is generally sufficient for bit rot, and MinIO does not recommend using the scanner for this type of health check.

web.title: mc admin rebalance - MinIO AIStor Documentation
web.description:
# mc admin rebalance
## [Anchor to: Description](https://docs.min.io/aistor/reference/cli/admin/mc-admin-rebalance/#description)  Description
The `mc admin rebalance` command allows starts, monitors, or stops a rebalancing operation on a MinIO AIStor deployment.

MinIO AIStor does not automatically rebalance objects when adding a new server pool. Instead, MinIO AIStor [writes new objects](https://docs.min.io/aistor/operations/scaling/expansion/#minio-writing-files) to the pool with relatively more free space compared to the other available pools on the deployment. Triggering a manual rebalancing procedure prompts MinIO AIStor to scan the entire deployment and move objects as necessary to achieve a similar available free space across all pools.

This is an expensive and time consuming operation. Consider only running a rebalance procedure during light or no use of the deployment. If write operations do occur during a rebalance operation, they process in parallel and write to a pool not actively in rebalancing.

You can stop a rebalance and start it again later as needed.

## [Anchor to: Syntax](https://docs.min.io/aistor/reference/cli/admin/mc-admin-rebalance/#syntax)  Syntax
### [Anchor to: mc admin rebalance start](https://docs.min.io/aistor/reference/cli/admin/mc-admin-rebalance/#mc-admin-rebalance-start)  mc admin rebalance start
#### [Anchor to: EXAMPLES](https://docs.min.io/aistor/reference/cli/admin/mc-admin-rebalance/#examples)  EXAMPLES
The `mc admin rebalance` command shifts objects from the pool with less free space to the pool with more free space so that there is roughly equal free space on both pools.
